Please review the code in functional-codebase. Then, review the blurb below. When you're done, in chat, please provide me with an initial attack surface mapping for this application.
Based on the [OWASP attack surface cheat sheet](https://cheatsheetseries.owasp.org/cheatsheets/Attack_Surface_Analysis_Cheat_Sheet.html), the attack surface of an application is:

1. the sum of all paths for data/commands into and out of the application, and
2. the code that protects these paths (including resource connection and authentication, authorization, activity logging, data validation and encoding)
3. all valuable data used in the application, including secrets and keys, intellectual property, critical business data, personal data and PII, and
4. the code that protects these data (including encryption and checksums, access auditing, and data integrity and operational security controls).
The following entry and exit points will contribute to the attack surface:

- UI forms and fields
- HTTP headers and cookies
- APIs
- Files
- Databases
- Other local storage
- Email or other kinds of messages
- Run-time arguments
- Application specific entry/exit points
Depending on its functionality or type of data it handles, it may fall into one of the following categories:

- Login/authentication entry points
- Admin interfaces
- Inquiries and search functions
- Data entry (CRUD) forms
- Business workflows
- Transactional interfaces/APIs
- Operational command and monitoring interfaces/APIs
- Interfaces with other applications/systems

 # Security Analysis
 
 ## Security requirements
 - Authorization controls
     - Registration should be controlled by admins only, not publicly.
     - Users should be assigned to courses and projects, and should only be able to access/post to those endpoints.
     - Mass downloads such as the comment manifest should be restricted to faculty and admins.
 
 ## Abuse cases
 - AC1: As an attacker, I want to be able to access high-privilege capabilities so that add other high-privilege users, edit/delete other user's posts, and access the moderation endpoint.
 - AC2: As an attacker, I want to be able to access credential information so that I can begin finding valid credentials of users with high-privilege capabilities.
 - AC3: As an attacker, I want to be able to serve malicious content so that I can deface the site or expand the attack to legitimate users.
 - AC4: As an attacker, I want to be able to remotely take down the site so that legitimate users can no longer access it.
 - AC5: As an attacker, I want to be able to craft malicious inputs so that I can get the application to return valuable information from the database.
 - AC6: As an attacker, I want to be able to gain information about the system so that I can better plan my attacks.
 - AC7: As an attacker, I want to be able to find sensitive information about users or the organization so that I can better plan my attacks.
 
 ## Attack trees
 ### AC1
 
 ### AC3
 
 ### AC4
 
 ## Attack surface mapping
 
 ## STRIDE threat modeling (DFD)
 
 ## Proposed mitigations
 ### CWE-1004 Sensitive Cookie Without 'HttpOnly' Flag
 Remove the .withHttpOnlyFalse() configuration.
 
 Relates to: AC3
 
 ### CWE-521 Weak Password Requirements (https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/521.html)
 Enforce stronger password requirements. For the purposes of this application, replace regex and error message to reflect at least 16 characters and at least one uppercase, lowercase, digit, and special character ().
 
 Regex: `^(?=.*[A-Z])(?=.*[a-z])(?=.*\d)(?=.*[^A-Za-z0-9])[^\r\n]{16,72}$` ([log-link])
 
 Relates to: AC2
 
 ### CWE-614 Sensitive Cookie in HTTPS Session Without 'Secure' Attribute (https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/614.html)
 N/A, false positive
 
 ### CWE-200: Exposure of Sensitive Information to an Unauthorized Actor (https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/200.html)
 Require authentication as an admin to reach the health endpoint.
 
 Relates to: AC6
 
 ### CWE-400 Uncontrolled Resource Consumption (https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/400.html)
 Implement rate limiting. For the purposes of this assignment, a simple custom filter-based rate limiter for something like 50 requests per minute (or less for demo purposes) seems appropriate (https://www.geeksforgeeks.org/advance-java/implementing-rate-limiting-in-a-spring-boot-application/).
 
 Relates to: AC4
 
 ### CWE-862 Missing Authorization (https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/862.html)
 Refactor code so that users must be added by administrators. Make only the login endpoint public-facing, and everything else must require authentication. For authorization, users should continue being separated by Role-Based Access Control (RBAC), but student/faculty users should also be explicitly assigned to courses and projects, and should only be permitted to access those endpoints.
 
 Relates to: AC7
 
 ### CWE-285 Improper Authorization (https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/285.html)
 While administrators should be granted high-privilege permissions, not all permissions are necessary to fulfill the role. An admin should not be permitted to change the contents of another user's existing post, or delete existing posts, as long as there is moderation functionality.
 
 Relates to: AC1, AC3
 
 ### CWE-204 Observable Response Discrepancy (https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/204.html)
 This vulnerability will be addressed by the proposed mitigation for CWE-862. As long as users can only be added by administrators, only administrators would receive confirmation of existing accounts, which is part of their expected high-privilege capabilities.
 
 Relates to: AC2
 
 ### CWE-79 Improper Neutralization of Input During Web Page Generation - Stored/Persistent XSS (https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/79.html)
 Sanitize post/comment body input using Java's HTML Sanitizer (https://owasp.org/projects/java-html-sanitizer).
 
 Relates to: AC3

 # The Research Blog & Project Discussion Board (Domain 4)
 
 This service coordinates collaborative project updates, announcements, and interactive comment feeds to streamline communication within active academic project teams and course groups.
 
 ## Functional Requirements
 Root Post Lifecycle Engine: Uniquely identify (UUID), initialize, and maintain the primary lifecycle of top-level communication feeds, categorized explicitly as either an official Academic Announcement or a Project Update Blog (storing title, rich text body content, categorization tags, and creation timestamps). To support multifaceted campus collaboration, root threads must accommodate hierarchical scoping rules: a discussion board or announcement feed can be bound directly to a single specific Project ID, a broad Course ID (encompassing multiple student projects), or an entire overarching Research Lab ID.
 
 Differentiated Nested Comment Threading: Process separate child comment response entries that attach to a specific root post ID. Comments are lightweight entities that do not contain title headers or categorization tags; they focus strictly on message strings, timestamp tracking, and author handles. To support multi-tiered discussions, comments must utilize a self-referential adjacency list model, where a comment can serve as a direct reply to a root post or a recursive reply to an existing comment.
 
 Moderation Pipeline & Status Management: Provide an administrative moderation workflow to enforce community standards across text inputs. The service must support state transitions (active, reported, hidden_by_moderator) applied independently to either root posts or child comments, allowing faculty roles to flag inputs and trigger cascading visibility adjustments across the board.
 
 Complex Multi-Field Query: Support robust text-search and filtering capabilities across the communication canvas. Users must be able to query and filter topics, blogs, and comments simultaneously using string keyword scans, timestamp ranges, specific author handles, target Project IDs, Course IDs, or Lab-specific project channels. The system must actively support targeted keyword searching and author filtering within individual comment streams.
 
 ## REST APIs
 
 Endpoint: /api/v1/discussions/posts
 Verbs: POST, GET
 Description: Create a primary announcement or blog post. Query parameters let users execute full-text keyword searches across post bodies or filter the entire portal communication feed by a specific Project ID, Course ID, Lab ID, or post category.
 
 Endpoint: /api/v1/discussions/posts/{post_id}
 Verbs: GET, PUT, DELETE
 Description: Read, update, and delete a primary announcement thread or project blog post.
 
 Endpoint: /api/v1/discussions/scopes/{scope_type}/{scope_id}/timeline
 Verbs: GET
 Description: Read a unified chronological workspace timeline aggregating all root announcements and team update blogs matching a specific structural context. (Note: {scope_type} accepts values restricted strictly to projects, courses, or labs to load the appropriate multi-project feed).
 
 Endpoint: /api/v1/discussions/posts/{post_id}/comments
 Verbs: POST, GET
 Description: Post an interactive comment response under a targeted primary announcement/blog thread. Read the full chronological JSON array of comments linked to that specific post. Downloading the full comment manifest in a single text file format for team archival audits must also be supported. Query parameters let users execute full-text keyword searches across comment bodies or filter by a specific author.
 
 Endpoint: /api/v1/discussions/posts/{post_id}/comments/{comment_id}
 Verbs: PUT, DELETE, GET
 Description: Edit, delete, or fetch a specific nested comment text record.

No UI forms, file-upload endpoint, email flow, or other external-system integration appeared in the reviewed application. File output is the comment-manifest download; local storage includes the H2 database file under `functional-codebase/data` and the Docker data volume.

### Valuable data and protective controls

- Account credentials and privileges: the database stores BCrypt password hashes and roles; user responses expose usernames, roles, and timestamps, not hashes. Bootstrap admin credentials are a deployment secret.
- Discussion content: posts/comments, authors, scopes, and timestamps may contain sensitive academic or personal information. DTO validation limits many field sizes; however, content is returned as supplied, and I found no server-side HTML sanitization in this code. Any client rendering this as HTML needs contextual output encoding/sanitization.
- Session and CSRF state: session-backed authentication and CSRF protection are present. The session cookie is configured `SameSite=Lax`; `SESSION_COOKIE_SECURE` defaults to `false`. The CSRF cookie is intentionally not HttpOnly, which makes client-side script compromise more consequential.
- Persistence: the default H2 file configuration has no application-level at-rest encryption setting. Protect the database file, Docker volume, and DB credentials through deployment permissions and secret management.

### Important exposure/control mismatches to track

1. **Anonymous registration is enabled**, and it creates student accounts. That conflicts with the admin-only registration requirement in [security-analysis.md](</C:/Users/wildm/Documents/Projects/cs763-wildman-final-project/cs763-wildman-final-project/security-analysis.md>).
2. **Discussion reads and the full comment text export are public.** The text format is on the same public GET route; this conflicts with the separate analysis requirement to restrict mass comment downloads. Hidden content is filtered from reads, but `REPORTED` content remains visible.
3. **Scope membership is not enforced in the reviewed model/service.** Scope IDs are user-supplied strings; authenticated users can post to an arbitrary project/course/lab ID, while public readers can query those feeds. The code applies role checks but shows no course/project assignment model or membership check.
4. **Admins can edit/delete other users’ content** through the author-or-admin check, contrary to the proposed restriction in the analysis document.
5. **Availability and audit surfaces:** feed/timeline queries load all posts and filter in memory, with no pagination visible; no application-level rate limit or audit logging was found in the reviewed Java sources. Request-size validation helps bound individual fields but not total feed/export size.
6. **Registration response discrepancy:** duplicate usernames return a conflict response, which reveals account existence to anonymous callers; login failures are generic.

Overall, the main exposed surface is a session-authenticated, role-based REST API whose read/search functions are deliberately public. The highest-value data paths are account creation/login, global discussion reads and export, content CRUD/moderation, and the persistent database/secret configuration.

 # Security Analysis
 
 ## Security requirements
 - Passwords must contain at least 16 characters with an uppercase letter, lowercase letter, number and special character.
 - All endpoints other than the login endpoint must require authentication, including GET requests.
 - Accounts must be delineated into role-based access control (RBAC) through admin, faculty, and student roles.
 - All account provisioning must only be controlled by admins.
 - Actuator endpoints must only be accessible by admins.
 - Faculty and student users must be assigned to courses and projects, and must only be able to access/post to those assigned endpoints.
 - Mass downloads such as the comment manifest must be restricted to faculty and admin roles.
 - All user input that may contain HTML markup (rich text) must be sanitized of malicious tags at the input stage.
 - Only the author of a post may be permitted to modify it. Even administrators may not modify other posts while moderation privileges are present.
 - Users must be restricted to no more than 50 API requests per minute.
 
 ## Abuse cases
 - AC1: As an attacker, I want to be able to access high-privilege capabilities so that add other high-privilege users, edit/delete other user's posts, and access the moderation endpoint.
 - AC2: As an attacker, I want to be able to access credential information so that I can begin finding valid credentials of users with high-privilege capabilities.
 - AC3: As an attacker, I want to be able to serve malicious content so that I can deface the site or expand the attack to legitimate users.
 - AC4: As an attacker, I want to be able to disrupt availability of the application so that legitimate users can no longer use it.
 - AC5: As an attacker, I want to be able to craft malicious inputs so that I can get the application to return valuable information from the database.
 - AC6: As an attacker, I want to be able to gain information about the system so that I can better plan my attacks.
 - AC7: As an attacker, I want to be able to find sensitive information about users or the organization so that I can better plan my attacks.
 
 ## Attack trees
 I tried to focus the contents of these attack trees on potentially exploitable weaknesses in the application, so there is not any focus in these trees on social engineering/physical security.

 See [AC4 Attack Tree in docs](functional-codebase/docs/Attack%20Trees%20PA2%20-%20AC4.png)
 
 Or: ![AC4 Attack Tree in docs](functional-codebase/docs/Attack%20Trees%20PA2%20-%20AC4.png)
 
 ## Attack surface mapping
 
 
 ## STRIDE threat modeling (DFD)
 
 ## Proposed mitigations
 ### CWE-1004 Sensitive Cookie Without 'HttpOnly' Flag
 Remove the .withHttpOnlyFalse() configuration.
 
 Relates to: AC3
 
 ### CWE-521 Weak Password Requirements (https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/521.html)
 Enforce stronger password requirements. For the purposes of this application, replace regex and error message to reflect at least 16 characters and at least one uppercase, lowercase, digit, and special character ().
 
 Regex: `^(?=.*[A-Z])(?=.*[a-z])(?=.*\d)(?=.*[^A-Za-z0-9])[^\r\n]{16,72}$` ([log-link])
 
 Relates to: AC2
 
 ### CWE-614 Sensitive Cookie in HTTPS Session Without 'Secure' Attribute (https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/614.html)
 N/A, false positive
 
 ### CWE-200: Exposure of Sensitive Information to an Unauthorized Actor (https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/200.html)
 Require authentication as an admin to reach the health endpoint.
 
 Relates to: AC6
 
 ### CWE-400 Uncontrolled Resource Consumption (https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/400.html)
 Implement rate limiting. For the purposes of this assignment, a simple custom filter-based rate limiter for something like 50 requests per minute (or less for demo purposes) seems appropriate (https://www.geeksforgeeks.org/advance-java/implementing-rate-limiting-in-a-spring-boot-application/).
 
 Relates to: AC4
 
 ### CWE-862 Missing Authorization (https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/862.html)
 Refactor code so that users must be added by administrators. Make only the login endpoint public-facing, and everything else must require authentication. For authorization, users should continue being separated by Role-Based Access Control (RBAC), but student/faculty users should also be explicitly assigned to courses and projects, and should only be permitted to access those endpoints.
 
 Relates to: AC7
 
 ### CWE-285 Improper Authorization (https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/285.html)
 While administrators should be granted high-privilege permissions, not all permissions are necessary to fulfill the role. An admin should not be permitted to change the contents of another user's existing post, or delete existing posts, as long as there is moderation functionality.
 
 Relates to: AC1, AC3
 
 ### CWE-204 Observable Response Discrepancy (https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/204.html)
 This vulnerability will be addressed by the proposed mitigation for CWE-862. As long as users can only be added by administrators, only administrators would receive confirmation of existing accounts, which is part of their expected high-privilege capabilities.
 
 Relates to: AC2
 
 ### CWE-79 Improper Neutralization of Input During Web Page Generation - Stored/Persistent XSS (https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/79.html)
 Sanitize post/comment body input using Java's HTML Sanitizer (https://owasp.org/projects/java-html-sanitizer).
 
 Relates to: AC3
